cost_notes: K fertilizer competition with Cs for plant uptake; highly variable by crop species and soil pH
Lime raises soil pH reducing Cs-137 availability to plants; most effective in low-pH podzolic soils of Polesie region
Buries Cs-137 below root zone; reduces external dose and crop uptake; but mobilizes deeper soil; also reduces dose rate by burial
Ferrocyanide and clinoptilolite (zeolite) added to intake water; very effective for Sr-90 in drinking water

Poland distributed KI to ~18 million people within days of accident; only European country to do so; reduced thyroid doses by estimated factor 3-10; USSR did NOT distribute to population in first days

If milk ban had been implemented in Belarus/Ukraine in first 2 months 1986: most thyroid cancer cases would have been prevented; ban was implemented TOO LATE in USSR (weeks delay); Germany France UK Austria all imposed bans
EU emergency limits 1986: 600 Bq/kg Cs-137 (most foods); 3000 Bq/kg (some categories); current long-term limits 600/1250 Bq/kg. Still applied to Chernobyl-origin goods
source: EU Council Regulation 3954/87; updated EC 733/2008; OECD-NEA Ch.VI

cost_notes: Sarcophagus (Shelter) built Nov 1986 by 90000 workers; reduced direct radiation and airborne release; not airtight; developed cracks; supplemented by NSC in 2016
NSC cost ~2.1 billion EUR (international funding); 108m high 162m wide 257m long; allows remote dismantling of sarcophagus; maintains negative pressure to prevent release
36-hour delay caused significant additional dose; if evacuated within 3-6 hours: estimated 3-4x more dose reduction achievable; delay due to Soviet secrecy
115000 evacuated from 30km zone over ~2 weeks; significant dose reduction for remaining exposures; long-term resettlement of >350000 people from 30km and Bryansk/Belarus zones 1986-1990
I-131 naturally decayed to negligible levels; within 2-3 months primary thyroid dose pathway gone; area contamination from Cs-137/Sr-90 persists indefinitely

5000t dropped (2400t lead + 1800t sand/clay + 800t dolomite + 40t boron) by ~1800 helicopter flights; partially suppressed fire but also compressed the core and temporarily INCREASED release in mid-April; fire extinguished ~9 May 1986
Despite countermeasures: 7-8% of Belarus small farm milk and 13-16% of other food still exceeded limits in 2005-2007; up to 90% of children in Narovlya District had body burdens >15 Bq/kg 1995-2007

400 workers tunneled under reactor in 15 days to install cooling heat exchanger; feared China Syndrome (corium melting through); turned out unnecessary as corium solidified; workers received significant doses
